transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started. We have two courtyard set options on the table for Soundstage 3 — a masonry build or a modular painted-timber approach — and I need to hear from each of you before I can sign off on a construction plan. We've got an approved budget of $180,000, and fabrication can't begin until we close out this design review. So let's go around the room: structural, permits, stunt, and insurance — what do you have for us?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical structural finding before we go further. My load test yesterday found that the masonry courtyard option would exceed Soundstage 3's 600 kilograms-per-square-meter floor limit. The modular painted-timber design does pass, but only if we install a 30-millimeter load-spreading deck. My written report is still working through the engineering queue, so I wanted to make sure this information is on the table now rather than waiting for the paperwork to clear.

transcript.text: I need to share what I confirmed with the local heritage-permit office this morning. The approved facade may be no wider than exactly 8 meters, and on-stage masonry cutting is prohibited. I should note that the permit clerk's email has not yet been added to the production file, but these constraints are confirmed and directly relevant to the masonry option we're discussing.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical stunt requirement before we settle on a design. My rehearsal assessment found that the scripted horse dismount requires an unobstructed lane exactly 10 meters long and 4 meters wide, with a 2-meter crash mat at its landing end. This lane needs to be factored into the courtyard layout now — the choreography note is still awaiting the next stunt meeting, but this constraint directly affects which set design and configuration we can approve.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical insurance finding before we proceed. I confirmed with the insurer's underwriter that our coverage excludes an open-flame brazier on this stage. However, an LED-flame prop is permitted under the policy, but only if it remains at least 12 meters from the sprinkler-head cluster and its certification is filed before filming. The endorsement is currently awaiting countersignature, so I wanted to make sure this constraint is on the table now as we evaluate the courtyard set design and any fire-effect elements that may be planned.
